story.title: Attacks on Grain Export Terminals Escalate in Black Sea Region
story.summary: Recent attacks on grain export terminals in the Black Sea have significantly impacted grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine. This escalation is part of an ongoing maritime conflict between the two nations, which threatens global grain supplies and reflects broader tensions over key shipping routes.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
timeline_highlights.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Warns Iran Over Strait of Hormuz Deal Deadline
timeline_highlights.summary: Donald Trump stated that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as early as Wednesday. He warned that if negotiations fail, Iran would face severe consequences. The situation follows Iran's increased control over the strait, where it has sought to impose tolls, a move not previously exercised before the conflict began on February 28.
key_facts: Trump indicated a potential deal for the Strait of Hormuz by Wednesday.
Iran has tightened its control over the strait and is seeking to charge tolls.
Trump warned of severe repercussions for Iran if negotiations fail.

timeline_highlights.title: Houthi Attack in Red Sea Results in Six Deaths, Including Three Pakistanis
timeline_highlights.summary: An attack by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels on a vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb strait has resulted in the deaths of six individuals, including three Pakistani nationals. This incident marks the first fatalities in the Red Sea related to such attacks in over a year. In response, US forces engaged a ship they claimed was attempting to breach a blockade of Iranian ports.
key_facts: Six people killed in Houthi attack on vessel.
Three of the deceased were Pakistani nationals.
This incident is the first fatality in the Red Sea from such attacks in over a year.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving the United States, Iran and Israel, centered on attacks, counterattacks and threats affecting Iran, neighboring states and maritime traffic in and around the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials said combat operations began on February 28, 2026, citing self-defense, protection of regional forces and allies, and freedom of maritime commerce; the United Nations has called for de-escalation, protection of civilians and compliance with international law.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The conflict’s current phase began on February 28, 2026. The United States notified the UN that it had commenced combat operations against Iran in cooperation with Israel; the UN Secretary-General also described subsequent Iranian attacks affecting Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz—between Iran and Oman, linking the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea—is a central theater because its security directly affects regional shipping and energy exports.

facts.label: Maritime and energy stakes
facts.value: Disruption to shipping through Hormuz has been a major international consequence: EIA reported that military action and the resulting de facto closure sharply reduced oil flows and contributed to large price increases in early 2026.

facts.label: Diplomatic and legal framework
facts.value: The UN has urged an immediate cessation of hostilities and stated that all parties must uphold the UN Charter, protect civilians under international humanitarian law and preserve nuclear safety. In the United States, the War Powers Resolution requires presidential consultation with Congress where possible and a written report within 48 hours when U.S. forces are introduced into hostilities without a declaration of wa

facts.label: Broader policy context
facts.value: The conflict occurs alongside longstanding international concern over Iran’s nuclear programme. UN Security Council Resolution 2231, adopted in 2015 to endorse the JCPOA, remains part of that background; the UN says earlier Iran-related Security Council measures were re-applied on September 27, 2025.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on late-July 2026 escalation, congressional war-powers action, Houthi-linked regional attacks, oil-market effects and ceasefire diplomacy; it does not attempt to document the conflict’s full military, humanitarian, diplomatic or legal history.

related_stories.summary: David McBride, a former Australian Army lawyer, has been released from prison after successfully applying for parole. He was sentenced in May 2024 to a maximum of five years and eight months for leaking military secrets related to Afghanistan, serving over two years of his sentence.

related_stories.title: Drone Strike on Passenger Train in Odesa Region Results in Fatalities
related_stories.summary: On August 13, 2026, a Russian Shahed drone struck a passenger train in the Berezivka district of Ukraine's Odesa region. The attack resulted in the deaths of the train driver and his assistant, while 340 passengers, including 67 children, were evacuated from the train.

related_stories.title: UN Reports Highest Civilian Deaths in Ukraine Since May 2022
related_stories.summary: The United Nations reported that civilian casualties in Ukraine reached their highest level since May 2022, with at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in July. This surge in casualties coincided with an increase in long-range missile strikes by Russia. The data was provided by the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission.
